questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.learningObjective: explain why a charge in a field follows a circular path
questions.stem: A revision sheet asks which statement best describes why a charged particle in a uniform field follows a circular path.

options.text: The magnetic force keeps pushing it forward along the direction of the field

options.text: The particle is always pulled inwards towards the source of the field

options.text: The magnetic force stays perpendicular to the velocity and supplies the centripetal force
The particle slows down and tightens its path into a spiral
options.misconception: believes the particle loses energy and spirals in

questions.explanation: The force is q v B, always at right angles to the velocity, so it acts as the centripetal force and bends the path into a circle. No work is done, so the speed stays constant.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.learningObjective: explain why the force on a wire scales with its current
questions.stem: Two students compare the reasoning behind a claim that doubling the current in a straight wire doubles the magnetic force on it.

answer.exemplar: The force on a straight conductor in a magnetic field is F equals I L B sin theta. Since the current appears as a single factor, doubling it while keeping the length, the field and the angle the same doubles the force. Nothing about the wire material or its cross-section enters the expression, so the scaling is strictly linear in current and would only be different for quantities such as the power dissipated in the wire.

questions.explanation: The force is proportional to the current through the factor I in I L B sin theta. With length, field and angle fixed, the relationship is strictly linear and no other term changes.
questions.hint: Find the current term in the formula.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.learningObjective: explain why a longer solenoid of the same turns is weaker
questions.stem: The checklist asks why a longer solenoid wound with the same total number of turns has a weaker field inside it than a short one.

answer.exemplar: The field inside a solenoid is B equals mu n I with n the number of turns per unit length. Two coils carrying the same total number of turns but of different lengths therefore have different turn densities, and the coil with the lower density gives the weaker field. To compare coils fairly you must hold turns per metre fixed rather than total turns, which is why the length of the winding always appears in this discussion.

questions.explanation: The relevant quantity is turns per metre, so the same total turns spread over a longer coil give a lower density and a weaker field. Comparing total turns alone would be misleading.
questions.hint: Compare turns per metre, not total turns.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_II
questions.learningObjective: explain why a field cannot add energy to a particle
questions.stem: The revision group explains why a magnetic field cannot be used to add energy to a charged particle.

answer.exemplar: The magnetic force is always perpendicular to the velocity of the particle, and work requires a force component along the displacement. Since that component is zero at every instant, the magnetic force does no work and cannot change the kinetic energy of the particle. A field can only redirect a particle, so any extra energy would have to be supplied by an electric field or by the source that maintains the magnet.

questions.explanation: Work needs a force component along the motion, and the magnetic force is perpendicular to the velocity at every point. It can change direction but never the kinetic energy.
questions.hint: Work needs force along the motion.
